content:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-10
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Karen Blake (Atlas CTO), Ravi Shah (Atlas ML Eng), Priya Rao (Infra Lead), Tom Li (Product)

Summary:
Quick sync on week-3 POC results. Focus: latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), throughput at different batching configs, and residual differences versus their baseline provider. Action items and next steps agreed for extended tail testing, cost spreadsheet, and on-prem network checklist.

Topics covered:
- High-level benchmark summary (Redwood vs baseline)
- Tail latency behavior and variance across regions
- Autoscale/batching tuning and cache effects
- Dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs for production throughput
- Security/SSO and VPC handoff questions

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: ok everyone thanks for joining, we know schedules are tight so we'll go straight into the numbers, Samir you wanna kick off with the topline?
[00:12] Samir: yeah sure, thanks Lena. Quick context — these runs are with the Atlas inference prompt set you provided last monday, 1k short prompts and 200 long prompts, mixed mix. Redwood run used H100-backed Dedicated instances with int8 quantization and prefix caching enabled. Baseline was run on VendorX managed endpoints, default server config.
[00:34] Karen: quick question, when you say prefix caching enabled, is that per-request kv cache or shared? we were seeing a lot of misses last week.
[00:41] Samir: that was shared per-model prefix/KV cache within a pool, so repeated prefixes hit the cache. but for the mix with highly varied prompts some misses still occur.
[00:53] Ravi: just FYI a few prompts have long embeddings prepended, that skewed p99 in our internal runs.
[00:58] Samir: noted. Ok numbers — average p50 latency for Redwood was 95ms across the 1k short prompt set, p95 ~180ms, p99 ~340ms. Baseline provider p50 ~140ms, p95 ~320ms, p99 ~610ms. So across the mixed workloads our p95 is about half of baseline which was the big headline.
[01:24] Tom: wait those p99 numbers look big — what was the sequence length distribution for that p99 bucket? are those the long prompts?
[01:30] Samir: mostly, yes. the long prompts are driving p99. when we remove the long prompt set p99 drops to ~420ms on Redwood and baseline to ~520ms. So long tails still a pain point.
[01:41] Karen: how did you measure throughput? this is tokens/sec or requests/sec?
[01:45] Samir: tokens/sec. peak sustained throughput on a single H100 node with our batching strategy was ~3.8k tokens/sec for the mixed set, pushing to ~12k tokens/sec if you batch aggressively for homogeneous short prompts. Baseline sustained about 2.1k tokens/sec under similar batching.
[02:05] Ravi: is that with forced batching at the service layer, or application-side accumulation? we'll likely not accept large request latencies to get throughput.
[02:12] Samir: we tested both. the 12k tokens/sec number assumes ~40ms added batching delay to aggregate small requests. for low-latency mode (<=50ms extra), throughput aligns closer to the 3.8k number. we can tune the batching window.
[02:26] Maya: and on cost — we produced a simple cost per 1M tokens estimate. Redwood Dedicated running optimized quantized model is coming in ~35% lower unit cost versus baseline for your expected mix, mostly from reduced GPU runtime and caching. I'll share the detailed spreadsheet after.
[02:42] Karen: 35% is promising. what assumptions are baked into that number? GPU price, preemptions, and network egress?
[02:48] Maya: assumptions are noted in the sheet. GPU hour at our reserved pricing, network egress included at 3% of total for embeddings calls which are small here. we did not include support fees or dedicated infra flat fees in that delta — we will add a fully-burdened view for procurement.
[03:04] Priya: on the private deployment side we need the exact firewall ports and CIDR ranges so our network team can pre-approve. can't move forward without that.
[03:11] Lena: understood. Priya we'll include that as an action item.
[03:14] Speaker 1: [inaudible] also we want to know the fallback behavior if a node is unhealthy, does traffic fall back to hosted?
[03:22] Samir: good point — our routing policy can failover to another pool in-region, or to a model variant with slightly higher latency but lower cost. failover to hosted plane? yes we can configure cross-tier fallback for the proof-of-concept but for production you'll likely want explicit canary policies.
[03:36] Ravi: any gotchas with quantization? some of our tests showed slight hallucination increase at int8 for the longer context.
[03:43] Samir: we saw minor token distribution changes at int8 in edge cases. for your golden prompts we ran A/B with float16 and int8 and the regression was within your evaluated thresholds, but we can run a more targeted quality regression for the 20 flagged prompts you sent.
[03:57] Karen: yeah please do, we need confidence before enabling aggressive quant.
[04:01] Samir: will do. Also note we tried an int4 prototype; that dropped latency but introduced non-trivial reg issues so we didn't include it in the headline numbers.
[04:12] Tom: can we talk about regional variance — you mentioned multiple regions?
[04:16] Samir: runs done in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. us-west-2 had slightly higher p95 by ~30ms due to instance placement variability during the test window. we saw consistent improvements versus baseline in all regions though.
[04:31] Priya: that variability worries our infra team for SLOs. How consistent are placements?
[04:36] Samir: placement is generally stable for dedicated reservations; there are edge cases during noisy-neighbor events. we can provide placement/trace logs for the runs we did.
[04:45] Lena: ok shifting to concrete next steps — Samir you'll run the extended tail test?
[04:49] Samir: yes, plan is to run 10k sample queries spread across three regions, capture full traces, and share histogram CSVs and raw logs. target end date 12/17.
[04:59] Ravi: for that test please include our full payload shapes including the embedding preamble, that last time you stripped some metadata and it changed timing.
[05:07] Samir: good call, we'll use the canonical payloads you drop in the shared folder.
[05:11] Karen: also, can you produce a per-route cost breakout? e.g. chat completion vs embeddings vs rerank?
[05:17] Maya: yep we will. the spreadsheet will have per-route unit costs, plus a blended cost for your expected traffic mix.
[05:23] Tom: what about security — SOC2, SSO, SIEM integration? we need to know how logs flow.
[05:29] Lena: we have SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO, and log export via secure syslog/S3. For Private there are options for KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys. we'll attach the security pack link after the call.
[05:42] Priya: perfect, can you also state retention defaults for transient logs? our policy is 90 days for detailed traces.
[05:49] Maya: retention defaults are 30 days in hosted; Dedicated includes options up to 365 days as an add-on. we'll list configurable retention in the pack.
[05:58] Speaker 2 (inaudible): any change in error rate?
[06:01] Samir: error rate was <0.1% for the Redwood runs, baseline had ~0.3% during their maintenance window. most errors were transient OOMs on large contexts for baseline.
[06:12] Karen: is tokenization parity guaranteed between providers? we had a mismatch early on that inflated tokens counted.
[06:18] Samir: good question — tokenization is model-specific; we matched the tokenizer to the open model variant in both runs. we can provide the canonical tokenizer hash for validation.
[06:27] Ravi: ok i'd like an item around validating token counts across providers.
[06:31] Lena: added.
[06:33] Samir: small note on autoscaling — Dedicated pools allow burst capacity; for sustained bursts you want committed nodes. autoscale times for spin-up were ~45-90s depending on region in our tests.
[06:44] Priya: 45-90s is a bit high for some use cases. is warm standby possible?
[06:49] Samir: yes warm standby with pre-warmed instances reduces spin-up to sub-15s but costs more. we can model tradeoffs in the cost sheet.
[06:57] Tom: any final concerns from Atlas side?
[07:00] Karen: just two: we need to see the extended tail results, and we need the private deployment network spec for approvals.
[07:07] Lena: we'll deliver both. quick note — i'll email a calendar invite for the network deep-dive slot week of 12/22 and share the cost spreadsheet by 12/15.
[07:16] Maya: also i'll attach the perf run artifacts link: https://drive.redwood/poc/atlas/perf-runs-2025-12-10.xlsx and the security pack: https://redwood.docs/security/atlas-pack.pdf
[07:29] Ravi: got it.
[07:31] Karen: thanks everyone.
[07:33] Lena: thanks all, talk soon.

Recap / Action items (as discussed):
- Samir to run extended 10k-sample tail-latency tests in us-east/us-west/eu and share raw logs + histograms (due 2025-12-17)
- Lena to share fully-burdened cost spreadsheet and per-route breakdown (due 2025-12-15)
- Priya to provide VPC/firewall matrix and data residency constraints (due 2025-12-19)
- Ravi to provide canonical payloads and the 20 flagged prompts for quality regression (due 2025-12-12)

References mentioned:
- Perf spreadsheet (link above)
- Security pack (link above)
- Internal run artifacts and traces (will be uploaded to the same shared folder)

Transcript notes: some words were auto-transcribed imperfectly (e.g., K-V cash, VendorX as Vender X), speaker labels may be slightly off in a few sections.

End of transcript.
